observations.text: SP recognized the assigned area only after the IP identified the boundary landmarks, and drifted 400 feet below the assigned altitude block before the correction was directed. Performance meets the desired standard for this introductory sortie but is marginal within it, since position was at no point confirmed independently by VOR/TACAN or GPS. Independent recognition of the area limits and of the assigned altitudes is expected to improve on the following sorties.

SP recognized the assigned area boundaries and maintained the assigned altitude block within 300 feet, requiring only the IP's verbal prompts and no direction of the flight path. Position relative to the area limits was confirmed on the GPS after prompting, and the turn back toward the area centre was flown without IP control inputs. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP identified the flight area characteristic points without assistance and remained within the assigned area throughout the working period, clear of the adjacent flight areas. A deviation of 220 feet from the assigned altitude and 8 degrees on the exit heading from the area reversal was recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP was aware of the area limits at all times, remained within the assigned characteristic points and did not approach the adjacent flight areas. The assigned altitude block was held within 120 feet, airspeed within 8 knots and the exit heading from each area reversal within 4 degrees, with position cross-checked on the TACAN at every turn. RTB was initiated accurately at the briefed fuel state without prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated precise awareness of the area limits, anticipating each boundary and reversing well inside the characteristic points, with no approach toward the adjacent flight areas. Deviations were negligible, with the assigned altitude held within 50 feet, airspeed within 5 knots and exit headings within 2 degrees, position being independently confirmed on both TACAN and GPS. SP additionally stated the RTB routing and the alternate airfield unprompted. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an area orientation scan that referenced only the ground features below the nose, did not correlate the aircraft's position with the flight area characteristic points. The area boundary was crossed without authorization and the assigned altitude block was exceeded by 400 feet, with the result that the IP had to direct the recovery turn and the return to the assigned area. Position confirmation by TACAN radial and DME at each reversal is required before the next sortie.

SP, due to lack of awareness of the aircraft's position relative to the area boundary, did not recognize the assigned area during the climbing reversal and continued outbound past the briefed characteristic point. The aircraft entered the adjacent flight area without authorization and the assigned altitude was exceeded by 350 feet, with the result that the IP took control and repositioned the aircraft. Study of the area chart and of the boundary landmarks must be repeated before the next sortie.

SP remained within the assigned area and recognized the boundary landmarks after the IP's verbal prompts, which meets the desired standard for this stage of training. Recognition and correction were applied with delay, the aircraft reaching 300 feet below the assigned altitude block and the exit heading from the reversal 10 degrees off. Marginal performance for the Training Section, since every recognition followed a prompt; unprompted awareness of the area limits is expected to develop over the following sorties.

SP was aware of the area limits and remained within the assigned characteristic points and altitudes throughout the working period, without entering the adjacent flight areas. A deviation of 200 feet from the assigned altitude and 12 knots in airspeed developed while the GPS was being used to confirm position, and was recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP maintained continuous awareness of the area limits, reversing at the briefed characteristic points and holding the assigned altitude block within 130 feet, airspeed within 9 knots and exit headings within 4 degrees. Position was confirmed on the VOR/TACAN without prompting and RTB was initiated at the briefed fuel state. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated exceptional area awareness, anticipating each boundary and completing every reversal with negligible deviations, the assigned altitude being held within 50 feet, airspeed within 4 knots and exit headings within 2 degrees. Position was independently cross-checked on TACAN and GPS at each reversal, and SP briefed the RTB routing and the alternate airfield to the IP without being asked. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an area entry flown without first identifying the briefed boundary landmarks, did not establish and maintain the assigned area after the first maneuver. The aircraft was allowed to climb 500 feet above the assigned altitude block on a heading toward the adjacent area, with the result that the IP directed the descent and the reversal back into the assigned area. Area familiarization and boundary landmark recognition are required before the next sortie.

SP, due to an attention bottleneck on the maneuver being practiced at the expense of the area position cross-check, did not monitor the aircraft's position relative to the flight area characteristic points. The area boundary was crossed without authorization and the assigned altitude was exceeded by 400 feet, with the result that the IP took control and repositioned the aircraft inside the assigned area. A deliberate position check between maneuvers must be established.

SP, due to judging the area limits by elapsed time rather than by the TACAN radial and DME, did not confirm the aircraft's position before each reversal. The assigned area was maintained only after the IP's verbal prompts, the altitude reaching 300 feet below the assigned block and the exit heading 10 degrees off before the deviation was recognized and corrected with delay. Position confirmation by navigation aid at each reversal is required.

SP, due to poor workload distribution, with navigation, communication and aircraft control attempted simultaneously, did not remain aware of the assigned area boundaries during the working phase. The drift toward the area limit was recognized only after the IP's verbal prompts, by which time airspeed was 20 knots low and the aircraft 300 feet below the assigned altitude block. The correction was applied with delay, without IP control inputs.

SP recognized and maintained the assigned area without IP's intervention, remaining clear of the adjacent flight areas at all times. Deviations of up to 250 feet from the assigned altitude block and 15 knots in airspeed occurred twice while position was being confirmed on the GPS, each recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Marginal performance for the Training Section, as both deviations arose from the same cause; a steadier altitude and airspeed cross-check while working the navigation aids is expected to improve.

SP was aware of the area limits at all times, reversed at the briefed characteristic points and remained within the assigned altitudes, using the TACAN to confirm position without prompting. Deviations did not exceed 140 feet in altitude, 9 knots in airspeed and 5 degrees on the exit headings, and RTB was initiated accurately at the briefed fuel state. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated precise area awareness throughout the sortie, positioning every maneuver so that the recoveries were completed well inside the area characteristic points. Deviations were negligible, with the assigned altitude block held within 50 feet, airspeed within 5 knots and exit headings within 2 degrees, position being independently confirmed on both VOR/TACAN and GPS. SP also stated the RTB and alternate airfield options unprompted when the weather in the area began to change. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an area orientation built on a single ground feature instead of the full set of briefed characteristic points, did not recognize the assigned area after the second reversal. The aircraft entered the adjacent flight area without authorization and climbed 450 feet above the assigned block, with the result that the IP took control and returned the aircraft to the assigned area. The area chart and its boundary points require further study before the next sortie.

SP, due to acceptance of the GPS depiction without an independent check of the TACAN radial and DME, did not detect that the area boundary had been mis-identified during the working phase. The aircraft was flown 3 nautical miles into the adjacent flight area without authorization and 400 feet outside the assigned altitude block, with the result that the IP directed the recovery and flew part of the repositioning. Cross-checking area position against a second navigation source is required.

SP, due to initiating each reversal only when the boundary landmark appeared abeam instead of anticipating it, did not remain within the assigned area limits with the briefed margin. The IP's verbal prompts were needed to start every recovery turn, and the assigned altitude reached 300 feet low with the exit heading 10 degrees off before the deviation was recognized and corrected with delay. Anticipation of the area limits by the briefed lead distance is required.

SP, due to an interrupted instrument cross-check while attention remained outside the cockpit on the area landmarks, did not hold the assigned altitudes and airspeed while remaining within the flight area. The deviation reached the limit of 300 feet in altitude and 20 knots in airspeed and was recognized only after the IP's verbal prompts, the correction being applied with delay. No IP control inputs were required.

SP, due to a position cross-check performed only at the end of each maneuver rather than continuously, did not anticipate the drift toward the area boundary during the working phase. The aircraft remained inside the assigned area, but the assigned altitude block was exceeded by 230 feet and the exit heading from the recovery turn was 8 degrees off. Both deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without IP's intervention.

SP, due to distraction by a radio call while re-establishing position within the flight area, did not monitor the assigned altitude block during the reversal. Altitude deviated by 240 feet and airspeed by 14 knots before the cross-check was resumed, the aircraft remaining well inside the assigned area limits throughout. The errors were recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without IP's intervention.

SP recognized and maintained the assigned area accurately and without prompting, used the TACAN and GPS to confirm position and remained clear of the adjacent flight areas. Deviations stayed within the desired standard at 140 feet in altitude and 9 knots in airspeed, but recurred on each of the three area reversals rather than being isolated. Marginal performance for the Training Section; tighter altitude and airspeed control during the area reversals is expected to improve with practice.

SP demonstrated exceptional area awareness, anticipating every boundary and characteristic point so that all maneuvers were completed well within the assigned area and altitudes. Deviations were negligible, with the assigned altitude held within 50 feet, airspeed within 4 knots and exit headings within 2 degrees, and position independently confirmed on VOR/TACAN and GPS at each reversal. SP briefed the RTB routing and the alternate airfield without being asked and initiated the recovery ahead of the briefed fuel state. Above end of block MIF achieved.
